title: AWS Step Functions to Amazon SageMaker AI confidence gate
description: An AWS Step Functions Choice state acts on the answers of an open-weight Strands Decider model on Amazon SageMaker AI only when it is confident; the rest go to Amazon SQS.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern deploys an AWS Step Functions Express workflow that calls an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint serving the open-weight Strands Decider decision model, directly through the AWS SDK integration. The model answers three typed questions about a support ticket in one call: a choice for the owning department, a score for urgency, and a yes/no question about an active security incident.

A Choice state is the confidence gate. A confident department answer is auto-routed. A suspected security incident is published to an Amazon SNS topic and still goes to a person. Everything else, including any ticket for which the model call failed or returned something unusable, goes to an Amazon SQS human-review queue with a dead-letter queue behind it.
The stack builds the model container image, so you need a container builder (Docker, or Finch with `CDK_DOCKER=finch`), and the account and Region must be bootstrapped with `npx cdk bootstrap`.

bullets.text: Call AWS services with Step Functions AWS SDK integrations
Custom inference containers for Amazon SageMaker AI

text: Run the three sample tickets in the `events` folder: a clear one is auto-routed, an ambiguous one goes to the Amazon SQS review queue, and a security one also sends a page to Amazon SNS.
See the GitHub repo for the commands and expected output.

Delete the endpoint log group that Amazon SageMaker AI creates: aws logs delete-log-group --log-group-name /aws/sagemaker/Endpoints/$ENDPOINT. Read $ENDPOINT from the DeciderEndpointName stack output before you delete the stack.
